newsitem.title: KENYA: Demand for shares seen lower at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Demand for shares seen lower at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Prices on average eased across the board at the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Tuesday on lower investor demand for shares and brokers said this was to be expected from a market that has generally remained depressed for months.

The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index lost 12.45 points to stand at 3036.72. Turnover was posted at 16.461 million shillings traded on 1,178,318 shares from 10.698 million shillings traded on 294,134 shares on Monday.
Turnover was boosted by 900,000 shares of sisal concern Rea Vipingo Plantations which were sold at 9.75 on the three-day special lots board, brokers said.
In financials, Barclays Bank eased to 96.50 from 99, Diamond Trust Bank lost a shilling to close at 35 from 36, while Standard Chartered Bank traded 12,100 shares at an unchanged 46.
"There was a slight increase in the supply of shares and a significant lack of demand in the market," a broker said.

"The drop in prices should not really come as a surprise as the market has been depressed for quite some time," he said. "Many investors have seen it prudent to cut off their losses and move on and are therefore offloading as many shares as possible."
Brokers said the increase in supply of shares could be from investors who wanted to cash in on their shares as the market went into the Christmas season and released their funds for private spending.
Carbacid Investments traded 100 shares at 115 from 88 shillings. Carbacid announced a bonus issue of three shares for five held on October 24, 1996.
Foreigners bought 2,400 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting Co at 121 from 120 and 48,472 shares of Kenya Breweries at 49.25 from 48.
